title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
Google’s AI advancements, including AI-native laptops and Gemini-powered features, are reshaping its product ecosystem. Simultaneously, Medicare is pioneering AI reimbursement for healthcare services, and Google and SpaceX are exploring orbital data centers for AI compute. Cybersecurity is receiving significant investment, exemplified by Exaforce’s $125 million Series B funding. However, a recent data breach underscores the risks associated with AI integration.

OpenAI and Microsoft’s revenue-sharing agreement—valued at $38 billion—reveals key financial dynamics within the AI sector. The European Central Bank is urging banks to prepare for AI-driven cyberattacks, while Bank of America issued a cautious outlook on potential Fed rate cuts. Nvidia’s presence in China, alongside former President Trump’s delegation, is a critical geopolitical factor impacting the AI chip market.

Globally, tensions remain high with escalating conflict in the Middle East and ongoing repercussions from the Iran war, including supply chain disruptions. Pakistan’s airstrike in Afghanistan has triggered calls for a war crimes investigation, and Ghana is preparing to evacuate its citizens due to anti-immigrant protests. The EU is considering measures to restrict children’s access to social media.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
Wall Street closed defensively on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 down 0.16% and the Nasdaq 100 declining 0.87%, largely due to hotter-than-expected April CPI data. The 10-Year Treasury Yield remained steady at 4.465%, while the US Dollar Index strengthened to 98.367 and crude oil decreased to 101.87. Gold experienced increased demand.

Overnight, Asian markets showed optimism, with the Nikkei 225 up 0.84%, the Hang Seng rising 0.15%, and the Shanghai Composite gaining 0.67%, fueled by Chinese property activity and anticipated trade discussions. European markets were cautious, influenced by weak German wholesale price inflation and rising French unemployment.

US futures are currently higher, with S&P 500 futures up 0.19% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.67%, indicating a rotation back into growth stocks. Key catalysts for today’s session include ongoing geopolitical tensions, the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting, and the continued impact of yesterday’s inflation data on bond yields and the dollar. The market is expected to trade range-bound with a slight upward bias.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The US market concluded Wednesday, May 13, 2026, with a nuanced performance driven by growth sector strength despite inflation concerns. The S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7444.3, while the Nasdaq 100 jumped 1.04% to 29366.943, reflecting continued tech appetite. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.14% to 49693.2. Trading volume was lighter than average, suggesting a retail-driven rally rather than broad institutional buying.

The “Fear Gauge” (VIX) remained subdued at 17.99, indicating controlled rotation and sector-specific gains. A notable divergence emerged, with Technology (XLK) surging 0.94% and Utilities (XLU) falling 1.15%, signaling investor preference for growth over safety. This rotation highlighted a willingness to take on risk for potential upside.

Inflation data played a key role, with a “hot” April PPI report triggering a slight decrease in the 10-Year Treasury Yield to 4.463%, despite market concerns. The US Dollar Index rose 0.20% to 98.38, reacting to the PPI data. Crude Oil prices fell 0.92% to $101.24, influenced by unexpectedly low inventory levels.

Within the Magnificent Seven, Nvidia led the gains, up 2.29%, while Microsoft edged down 0.63%. Alphabet, Meta, and Tesla also saw significant increases, reflecting continued investor confidence in the long-term growth potential of these tech giants. The market’s focus remains on digesting inflation data and anticipating the Federal Reserve’s response.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
The Iran-US conflict ceasefire is unstable, with President Trump criticizing Iran’s counteroffer as “unbelievably weak,” threatening renewed conflict and driving up global energy costs. US inflation has surged to 3.8%, largely due to the conflict’s impact on energy markets. eBay rejected a $55.5 billion offer from GameStop, citing financing concerns.

Meanwhile, in Eastern Europe, Andriy Yermak is under investigation for money laundering in Ukraine’s anti-corruption probe. The US is pursuing the establishment of new military bases in Greenland, signaling a strategic focus on Arctic influence. 

A strike in Afghanistan reportedly killed 269 Afghans, prompting international scrutiny and calls for investigation. The European Union has imposed sanctions on Israeli settlers due to escalating violence in the West Bank. 

These developments highlight the interconnectedness of geopolitical instability and economic repercussions, with the potential for a significant global economic downturn if the Iran-US conflict escalates. Monitoring Tehran’s response to Trump’s comments and global oil benchmarks is crucial.
